belief: Only healthy, strong people can serve God well.
origins: Church culture often celebrates energetic, visible service. Those with chronic illness or limits may feel their service is inferior or unseen.
teaches: “God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.” “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Peter and John, “unschooled, ordinary men,” astonished the council because “they had been with Jesus.” Epaphroditus served “nearly unto death.” Paul wrote letters from prison. God values faithfulness, love, and prayer, and often shows His power most through the weak.
errors: Believing service is either strong or worthless.
Predicting that my service is useless.
Feeling weak and concluding I cannot serve well.
questions: What has God done through weak people in Scripture?
What acts of service are within my reach?
How has my weakness made me more compassionate?
What do I admire in the quiet servants I know?
What does Scripture say about God’s power in weakness?
What is one way I can serve this week?
truth: God does not need strong servants. He uses weak ones to show His power. My faithfulness, prayers, and love count as real service.
hw_truths: His power is perfected in weakness.
Ordinary people with Jesus do great things.
log: Each week, note one act of faithful service.
actions: Say it when you feel weak.
prayer: Lord, use me in my weakness. Thank You that Your power is made perfect there. Help me serve faithfully with what I have. Amen.
